newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on weather, spreads.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on weather, spreads.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended lower on Thursday with new crop down on forecasts for continued good crop weather and on bull spreading ahead of Friday's USDA Supply and Demand Report, traders said.
"We sort of ran into a buying vacuum after the run-up we've had the last few days," said Ann Frick, analyst with Prudential Securities.
"We still have a very good outlook for weather which is weighing on the new crop and there is an expectation that we'll see an increase in the new crop ending stocks tomorrow."
USDA will release its report at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT.
Analysts expect USDA will leave old crop ending stocks about unchanged at 130 million bushels but raise new crop supplies from last month's estimate of 240 million to account for increased acreage.
Weather continued to weigh on new crop futures. The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook called for above normal precipitation and below normal temperatures.
That scenario was considered ideal for crop development as soybeans bloom.
Soybeans ended 11-3/4 to two cents per bushel lower with August down two at $7.46.
